title: Collapse tool handler/freshness pairs into ToolContext seam
description: Introduce ToolContext { db, workspace_root, annotate_freshness } passed to tool handlers. Collapse handle/handle_with_freshness pairs into single functions. Add FreshnessCounts annotator used uniformly. Fold the mcp.rs four-line ritual (require_analysis/resolve_workspace/get_db/wrap_response) into one helper on SutraServer. Wide but shallow — mechanical edits across tools/ and mcp.rs, contract tests unaffected (JSON shape unchanged).
execution_record: Introduced ToolContext (tools/mod.rs) + FreshnessAnnotator (freshness.rs). Collapsed handle/handle_with_freshness pairs into handle/handle_ctx/handle_inner in 5 modules (map, grep, find, hotspots, file_health). Migrated all 22 standard mcp.rs handlers to tool_context() + ctx.wrap(). Fixed double workspace resolution. Two commits: 72b20f6, e7e6538. All 732 tests pass.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex review (adversarial-review, base=32a88fb):

Verdict: needs-attention

Finding (medium): ToolContext snapshots response freshness at request start, not wrap time.
- `tool_context()` computes `response_freshness` up front; `ctx.wrap(result)` copies that cached value.
- Old `wrap_response()` called `self.freshness(db)` after the handler completed.
- For long-running handlers overlapping a parse, top-level `is_stale`/`as_of`/`parsing_in_progress` can now describe request start instead of response time.
- Recommendation: compute freshness at wrap time, not context creation time.

Convention violations (from sutra_review): SutraServer::await_parse is async but not pub and doesn't return Result (breaks two FCA conventions, confidence 0.97).

Health degradation: find.rs handle_inner 7.2→6.04, file_health.rs handle_inner 6.69→5.53 (both hotspot-driven).
